title: ForestLab: a vote with an auditable membership list
excerpt: A hard-vote fraction can look reassuring while hiding which models saw the observation. This project exposes every bootstrap count, path, leaf and vote, then excludes in-bag trees before calling a prediction OOB. No estimator library or model API does the fitting.
headings: ForestLab: a vote with an auditable membership list
V0.2: break a pairing, freeze the model

title: GameLab: minimax value is unique, the strategy may not be
excerpt: A multi-agent score table can be cyclic. A single average payoff can look balanced even when both policies are exploitable. Even an exact game value need not identify one optimal randomized policy. GameLab makes those distinctions inspectable for a supplied small zero-sum matrix, rather than hiding degeneracy behind a single solver vector.
headings: GameLab: minimax value is unique, the strategy may not be

title: GraphLab: audit what the graph contributes
excerpt: Two-layer GCN from scratch with exact input-margin gradients and budgeted single-edge deletion sensitivity. Input locality differs from graph normalization: node 3 has zero feature gradient for node 0, yet deleting edge 2-3 changes its margin by +0.016852 after degree renormalization.
headings: GraphLab: audit what the graph contributes
Exact audits and an exact limitation
Edge deletion is a different question

title: GroundCheck
excerpt: A citation is not evidence. GroundCheck exposes the lexical machinery behind that distinction in a complete, editable provenance inspector.

title: HallLab
excerpt: Tiny constraint-based AI assignment, with every supported variable/value backed by a complete injective assignment and every rejected edge explained by a forced-residual Hall obstruction. A full synchronous pairwise-AC baseline makes the global bottleneck visible.
headings: HallLab: distinct is a global promise
HallLab: local support is not a shared solution
HallLab: every minimal conflict, every minimal removal
HallLab0.4: a spare value is not a cycle

title: HamiltonLab: a high acceptance rate can hide a trapped chain
excerpt: A chain can accept almost every proposal and still miss half the target. Dependency-free Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with explicit leapfrog energy errors, reversible integrator checks, log-domain Metropolis decisions and complete transition histories.
headings: HamiltonLab: a high acceptance rate can hide a trapped chain
Quadratic resonance: stable, accepted and barely moving
Rank-normalized split and folded chain checks
Analytic harmonic flow and mass convention
Finite-window observables: a mean can cancel while magnitude stays stuck
Random durations: zero position correlation is not independence

title: HingeLab
excerpt: Exact rational ReLU regions and class-change topology.

title: HornLab
excerpt: Bounded positive propositional Horn inference with synchronous derivation rounds and every indexed rule decision. Compare the least model with every classical and supported model: a supported circular assignment need not have a derivation.
headings: HornLab: a circle is not a proof
HornLab: deletion has a derivation debt

title: InfluenceLab: differentiate a weight, then actually delete the row
excerpt: Convex logistic influence functions with converged Newton fits and full Hessian/solve witnesses. The deletion-path extension refits continuously along selected weight changes, then checks integrated local derivatives against actual endpoint loss.
headings: InfluenceLab: differentiate a weight, then actually delete the row

title: KernelLab: exact conditioning, explicit uncertainty assumptions
excerpt: Dependency-free Python, 43 Python tests, four Node/Chrome tests, fit/predict/response JSON CLI, reproducible SVG and Python 3.10-3.13 CI. Standard GP theory, no new method.
headings: KernelLab: exact conditioning, explicit uncertainty assumptions

title: Kurdistan International Sociological Association website — case study
excerpt: Trilingual website (English, Sorani Kurdish right-to-left, and Kurmanji Kurdish) for KISA, an academic association for sociologists of Kurdistan and the Kurdish diaspora. Built with Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind, exported as static HTML and hosted on Cloudflare.
headings: Kurdistan International Sociological Association website — case study
Worked example: publishing a news post

title: KVLens
excerpt: A cache is state, not a shortcut in the answer. This offline project implements one untrained causal multi-head attention block and checks its actual logits, every retained key/value, absolute position and counted operation against four independently executed paths.
headings: The comparison needed a stronger baseline
Fix the state bug, then test the lifecycle

title: LatentLab
excerpt: A trained Gaussian variational autoencoder whose reconstruction, latent regularization and prior generation can be inspected separately.

title: loglens — case study
excerpt: Dependency-free access-log analysis for incident work: point it at an nginx/Apache combined log or structured JSON logs and get the numbers that matter in the first five minutes of an incident — error rate, status distribution, hottest paths, hottest failing paths, and the source IPs behind 5xxs.
headings: The constraint that shaped the build
Worked example: the first five minutes of a 5xx spike

title: LoRALab: same model, different factor-SGD step
excerpt: LoRALab implements low-rank adaptation in dependency-free Python, then exposes a less obvious distinction: equivalent factor coordinates can represent the same model but take different ordinary SGD steps. The browser and Python evaluators are independent. This is an arithmetic diagnostic on a synthetic classifier, not a new optimizer or an LLM benchmark.
headings: LoRALab: same model, different factor-SGD step
Every original epoch boundary stays attached

title: MarginLab: keep the constraints visible
excerpt: Manual linear/RBF soft-margin SVM learning with replayable pair updates and editable30-feature scores.
headings: Exact feasibility before an exact bound

title: Personal site — midya.ca — case study
excerpt: Personal site, live at midya.ca. Built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js, deployed as a static build on DigitalOcean App Platform. The background is a procedural galaxy rendered in WebGL — nothing is loaded from outside the code: the stars, spiral galaxy, dust, constellation lines, and nebula haze are all generated at runtime.
headings: Worked example: updating the site's copy

title: MixtureLab
excerpt: Manual Gaussian-mixture EM on real, licensed chemistry. Likelihood is not identity.

title: MoeLab: mixture-of-experts from scratch, routing measured
excerpt: A mixture-of-experts layer routes each input to one (or a few) specialized sub-models instead of running one dense network over everything. MoeLab implements the whole mechanism in dependency-free Python - router, experts, sparse training objective, load-balancing term - and treats routing behavior as something to measure, not assume.
headings: MoeLab: mixture-of-experts from scratch, routing measured
Measured results (checked-in fixture, pinned in tests)
The aux-loss finding nobody puts in the README

title: ParticleLab
excerpt: A particle filter can report equal weights and full effective sample size while carrying duplicate descendants of one badly placed initial particle. Weight ESS measures concentration of weights, not whether the state distribution has enough support. A single tidy score can hide lost uncertainty.
headings: Static square symmetry and sign loss
Retrospective paths and missing early uncertainty
Backward simulation still depends on finite support
Condition the proposal, keep the approximation honest
